title: A new PIN that was saved can be followed by words saying the number check ran out
what: Forgot your PIN saves the new PIN and then signs the person in as a second step. If the internet drops between the two, the person sees an internet error with the PIN boxes still open. Tapping the button again is refused because the number check was already used up by the first save, so the card says the check ran out (or, in the older way, that the code is wrong) and sends the person back to check the number again. Nothing ever says the new PIN is already saved and works.
expected: After the PIN is saved, a failed sign-in says the new PIN is saved and offers to sign in with it, without asking for the number check again.
who: owners and staff who forgot their PIN
how_often: rare: only when the internet drops between the two steps
fix_line: Remember that the PIN was saved and retry only the sign-in

title: The hidden anti-robot box does nothing in the send-a-code way of Forgot your PIN
what: Both forgot-PIN cards carry a hidden box that only a robot fills in, so the server can drop the ask. In the Verify with WhatsApp way its value is sent. In the older way, where MettleUp sends a code, the value is collected but an empty value is always sent instead, so a robot is never caught by it there. That older way is off while Verify with WhatsApp is on.
expected: The hidden box value is sent with the ask in both ways.
who: MettleUp (wasted WhatsApp sends), not gym users
how_often: every ask in the send-a-code way, when that way is switched on
fix_line: Pass the hidden box value along with the ask for a code

title: Sign out of this device tells everyone they need a new code to come back, even with a PIN
what: The question before signing out says: to come back, sign in with your mobile number and a new code, which an owner makes. A plain sign-out does not clear the PIN, so anyone with a PIN comes back with the number and the PIN. A front desk person reading this may think they are locked out until the owner is there, or ask the owner for a code they do not need.
expected: With a PIN set the words say to come back with the mobile number and the PIN; the new-code words show only for someone with no PIN.
who: owners, staff and trainers who have a PIN
how_often: every sign-out by a person with a PIN
fix_line: Choose the words by whether this person has a PIN
